items.followUp: Why do noble gases have very low chemical reactivity?

rubric.why: Noble gases are stable because their outermost electron shell is complete.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the complete outermost shell or stable electronic configuration.

rubric.why: Their stable configuration means they have little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.
rubric.how: Award for stating that noble gases do not readily gain, lose, or share electrons.

modelAnswer: Noble gases have a complete outermost electron shell, so they have a stable electronic configuration.
They have little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons; therefore, they are not reactive.

items.followUp: How does shielding affect the ionisation energy of an atom?

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons shield outermost electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for stating that inner-shell electrons shield the outermost electrons from the nucleus.

rubric.why: Shielding reduces the nuclear attraction on outermost electrons, making their removal easier and cation formation more likely.
rubric.how: Award for linking reduced attraction to easier removal of outermost electrons or more ready cation formation.

modelAnswer: Inner-shell electrons shield the outermost electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus.
The outermost electrons are held less strongly and are removed more easily, so cations form more readily.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?

rubric.why: Ionic compounds consist of oppositely charged ions arranged in a lattice.
rubric.how: Award for identifying positive and negative ions or their arrangement in a crystal lattice.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attraction holds the ions firmly in position, giving the compound its solid state.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that strong forces between the ions hold them firmly together.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions arranged in a crystal lattice.
Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions hold them firmly in fixed positions, so ionic compounds are solids.
